Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

{"visible_record": {"initial_information_actually_supplied": "A 28-year-old man presented with circulatory shock. At 08:21 on Day 0, BP was 70/45 mmHg and heart rate 142 beats/min. Right-heart abnormalities and a femoral venous thrombus were identified. VA-ECMO started at 10:20. CT pulmonary angiography at 11:58 showed main/branch pulmonary arterial filling defects. These are extracts for a retrospective ICU record review, not a live treatment instruction.

Day-0 record:
Time | Record
11:55 | Sample: platelets 21 × 10⁹/L, haemoglobin 150 g/L, fibrinogen 1.18 g/L and aPTT 43.5 s. Result-reporting times are not supplied for this sample.
14:50–15:10 | Two institutional therapeutic doses of apheresis platelets were transfused. Other haemostatic support was recorded over 13:15–17:00.
17:00 | Unfractionated heparin (UFH) was paused and the first alteplase infusion started. No post-transfusion platelet count immediately before this infusion is supplied.
17:20 | Arterial cannulation-site bleeding was treated with compression.
17:39 | Sample: platelets 62 × 10⁹/L, haemoglobin 136 g/L, fibrinogen 1.38 g/L and aPTT 47.5 s. Result-reporting times are not supplied for this sample.
18:10 | Vasoactive infusion rates were reduced, but ECMO and vasoactive support were still needed.
19:03 | A progress note records cessation of cannulation-site bleeding after compression; a second alteplase dose was ordered.
19:25 | The second infusion started. Each infusion stage lasted approximately one hour; exact completion timestamps are unavailable.
20:13 | A coagulation sample was obtained: fibrinogen 1.07 g/L and aPTT 58.9 s.
21:06 | The coagulation results from the 20:13 sample were reported.

The treating team later reported that UFH restarted after the second infusion, approximately one hour after its 19:25 start. No independent exact restart timestamp is available. A patient-specific anticoagulation target and the documented evidence used at restart are not supplied. Do not prescribe a regimen, convert unverified infusion rates, invent an exact completion/restart time, or infer safety from an outcome not supplied.", "audience": "Clinical team", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Timing
Recorded times: second alteplase infusion started 19:25; coagulation sample drawn 20:13; results reported 21:06. Derived times: each infusion lasted approximately one hour, so estimated completion is 20:25; the team reported UFH restarted approximately one hour after the 19:25 start, giving an estimated restart of 20:25. The 20:13-to-report delay is 53 minutes. The estimated restart preceded the 21:06 report, so the aPTT 58.9 s result could not have informed the restart decision. Uncertainty remains because no independent exact restart timestamp exists.

Evidence and risks
The 11:55 platelet count (21 × 10⁹/L) is recorded. Two apheresis platelet doses were transfused 14:50–15:10. No post-transfusion count immediately before the 17:00 first alteplase is supplied, so the platelet count at first alteplase initiation is unknown. The 17:39 count (62 × 10⁹/L) is recorded but cannot be attributed solely to transfusion effect; confounders include consumption, dilution, and ongoing thrombosis. Fibrinogen fell from 1.38 to 1.07 g/L between 17:39 and 20:13, and aPTT rose from 47.5 to 58.9 s, suggesting progressive coagulopathy during alteplase.
